clue.text: Jill's reassuring words after tumble in film?

definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme Jack fell down and Jill came tumbling after, so her comforting line would tell her companion she is unhurt
a 1959 Boulting brothers comedy about trade unions and management

explanation.surface: A question about what Jill said to Jack once they had both fallen down the hill, offered as a movie title.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme has Jack falling first and Jill 'came tumbling after', so 'after tumble' sets her speaking once she has landed. The words are also the title of a classic British satire.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a reassurance that one is unhurt (addressed to the boy in the rhyme) and the title of a celebrated British comedy picture.

clue.text: Envoy in a muddle when presented to English Queen

indicators.note: these words place the first piece before the abbreviations that follow it

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword Queen

explanation.surface: A diplomat gets flustered on being introduced to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link: the envoy is in a mess when presented to English ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A messenger carries word on someone's behalf, just as an envoy is sent with a diplomatic communication.

clue.text: The smallest amount is permitted when inside

indicators.note: the word just before, when, is placed within the word for permitted

parts.note: as can mean when (as I left = when I left)

explanation.surface: A rule saying a minimum quantity is allowed only indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of little, meaning the tiniest quantity or degree possible.

clue.text: Nijinsky perhaps lost footing in shoe -career ruined

indicators.note: ruined tells us the letters of the trimmed shoe and career are wrecked and rebuilt
the word shoe loses its foot, i.e. its last letter, as the clue is written down the grid

explanation.surface: Someone slipped because of their footwear, and their whole working life was wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost footing' cuts the E from SHOE to give SHO; 'ruined' shuffles SHO with CAREER. Nijinsky here is not the dancer but the 1970 Triple Crown-winning horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Nijinsky was a famous thoroughbred that won the English Triple Crown, so it is an example of a racing animal.

clue.text: See blood surrounding head of goat in canyon

indicators.note: the word for blood is placed around the letter that follows
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A grisly sight of blood around a goat in a ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a link word inviting the solver to look at the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A gorge is a deep narrow valley with steep rocky sides, much like a canyon.

clue.text: Thieves duck coming to part of roof that sticks out

indicators.note: the duck arrives at the next piece, which follows it

parts.note: the teal is a small freshwater duck

parts.words: part of roof that sticks out
parts.note: eaves are the edge of a roof overhanging the walls

explanation.surface: Burglars who arrive on a rooftop, alongside a wildfowl perched on the overhang.
explanation.walkthrough: TEA LEAVES is Cockney rhyming slang for thieves (tea leaf = thief), a London usage.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang a tea leaf is a thief, so the plural stands for robbers.

clue.text: Strange article defending made-up story

indicators.note: the article guards the story by surrounding it

parts.note: a lie is a fabricated tale

explanation.surface: An odd piece of journalism that stands up for a fabrication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a newspaper piece, but it is the grammatical article AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien as an adjective means foreign or unfamiliar, i.e. odd or weird.

clue.text: Like charitable Communist

explanation.surface: A comparison with a generous left-wing politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' looks like a verb or preposition, but here it is an adjective meaning similar.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred as an adjective means similar or related, as in kindred spirits.

clue.text: A fellow snubbed after church dance

indicators.note: the A and the shortened fellow come after the church abbreviation
snubbed suggests a snub, i.e. a short nose, so the word is cut short at its end

explanation.surface: A man is cold-shouldered at a dance following a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snubbed' docks the last letter of CHAP to give CHA.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha is a lively Latin American ballroom routine.

clue.text: Plant a very large number by entrance to apartments

indicators.note: by means beside, so the next piece is placed next to the first

parts.note: a host is a great multitude

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A potted plant and a crowd of people by the doorway of a block of flats.
explanation.definitionFit: The hosta is a shade-loving garden perennial grown for its leaves.

clue.text: Flower people next to vehicle

explanation.surface: A bloom alongside a crowd and a car, perhaps at a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'next to' is a link here: the people go next to the vehicle, in that order.
explanation.definitionFit: The carnation is a common buttonhole bloom of the pink family.

clue.text: Teach wrongly about male cat

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the pronoun for a male
taught wrongly, the letters of teach are jumbled

explanation.surface: Giving a wrong lesson about a tomcat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teach' looks like the action of the surface, but it is fodder: 'wrongly' gives the arrangement CETAH, which 'about' wraps round the male pronoun after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheetah is a big spotted feline, the fastest land animal.

clue.text: Girl from east New Orleans, not south

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the remaining letters
the S, abbreviation for south, is dropped from the city name

explanation.surface: A young woman who hails from the eastern side of the Louisiana city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Orleans' reads as the city, but 'New' is the anagram signal working on the city's second word once 'not south' strips its final letter; the rearranged letters follow the compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleanor is a female given name, so it can stand for any lass.

clue.text: Annoy Ryder Cup captain losing first

indicators.note: the surname drops its initial letter

parts.note: Bernhard Langer, the German golfer, captained Europe's Ryder Cup team in 2004

explanation.surface: Upsetting the golf team leader who has just lost his opening match.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ryder Cup is the biennial golf contest between Europe and the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to anger is to irritate or make someone cross.

clue.text: As good as gold? Not us!

definitions.text: As good as gold? Not us!

parts.words: As good as gold? Not us!
parts.note: those who come second in a contest take silver, not the gold medal, so they would admit they are not as good as the winners

explanation.walkthrough: 'As good as gold' suggests well-behaved children, but it refers to medals: second place gets silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who finish just behind the winner, the second-placed competitors, receive silver rather than gold.

clue.text: Mended? Torn sofas may need to be

definitions.meaning: mended in the sense of got well again after illness

definitions.text: Torn sofas may need to be
definitions.meaning: ripped upholstery may need fresh fabric put over it again

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both regained health and given new upholstery, re-covered.

clue.text: Skip about playfully getting gash and nasty scrape

indicators.note: nasty suggests something mangled, so the letters of scrape are messed up

explanation.surface: A child skipping around gets a cut and a bad graze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' and 'and' are links; 'nasty' rearranges SCRAPE as CAPERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To frolic or leap about in a lively, playful way is an idiom for skipping around.

clue.text: Considerable mistake making journey there and back

parts.note: a round sum is a considerable one
a trip is a slip or mistake

explanation.surface: A big error on an outward and return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A return excursion that goes out and comes home again.

clue.text: Australian brings in good books for binding

indicators.note: the word for Australian takes in the abbreviation for good

parts.note: Strine is the Australian accent or vernacular
NT, New Testament, is a collection of books

explanation.surface: An Australian takes some good books to the bindery.
explanation.walkthrough: STRINE is a jokey name for Australian English, from 'Australian' said in that accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringent rules are strict, i.e. obligatory and firmly enforced.

clue.text: Check fixed support

explanation.surface: Inspecting a firm brace.
explanation.definitionFit: A check is a reverse or hindrance to progress.

clue.text: One wicket defeat

definitions.meaning: in cricket a wicket is made of three upright posts, and this is one of them
to baffle or beat someone with a hard question

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both one upright of a cricket wicket and, as a verb, to baffle or flummox.

clue.text: Customer for boatman?

definitions.meaning: slang for a client or customer
someone who propels a flat-bottomed boat with a pole

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a paying client and one who poles a flat boat on a river.

clue.text: Violent storm encountered on way back -nuisance

indicators.note: returning, so the word for encountered is read backwards

explanation.surface: A ferocious gale was met on the journey home, a real nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a severe gale or squall.

clue.text: Mother holding head of blind snake

indicators.note: the word for mother holds the next letter inside it
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A mother clutching a blind serpent.
explanation.definitionFit: The mamba is a venomous African serpent.

clue.text: Hearing test

definitions.meaning: a court hearing of a case

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a court case heard before a judge and a try-out or experiment.

clue.text: A group working in desert

parts.note: on means working, as with a machine switched on

explanation.surface: A team of people at work in arid wasteland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert is to forsake or leave behind.

clue.text: Superior, British in flying boat

indicators.note: the abbreviation for British goes inside the rearranged letters
flying suggests the letters of boat are sent off in a new order

explanation.surface: A British person aboard a flying boat, travelling first class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying boat' looks like a seaplane, but 'flying' rearranges BOAT as ABOT, with B put in.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a monastery is the monks' religious Superior.

clue.text: Truce in Crimea, it's fragile

indicators.note: fragile hints that the letters shatter and are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A ceasefire in a Black Sea peninsula conflict is shaky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; 'fragile' rearranges CRIMEA ITS.
explanation.definitionFit: An armistice is a ceasefire agreed between warring sides.

clue.text: Lighter empty, needing bit of gas injected

indicators.note: the letter is put inside the word for empty
a bit of a word here is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cigarette lighter has run dry and needs refilling with fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' is not a cigarette lighter but a flat-bottomed boat used to unload ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a flat-bottomed cargo boat, just like a barge.

clue.text: Having pep talk as part's cast for Beckett play

indicators.note: cast suggests the letters are thrown and re-formed, as well as a theatrical cast

explanation.surface: Actors get an encouraging speech as their roles are assigned for a Beckett production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having' and 'for' are links; 'cast' rearranges PEPTALKASPARTS. The S of 'part's' counts as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a one-act drama by Samuel Beckett in which an old man listens to recordings of himself.
